marker: # ref_size is the product length measured in the Ames Ancestor assembly GCA_000008445.1 by in
# silico PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. Every locus gives
# exactly one product, all are searchable at word size 11, none needs the rescue pass and none
# has a primer mismatch. The six chromosomal loci lie on AE017334.2, pXO1-aat on pXO1
# (AE017336.2) and pXO2-at on pXO2 (AE017335.3), as their names state.
# IMPORTANT: THE COPY NUMBERS BELOW ARE NOT PUBLISHED VALUES. The source table carries
# primers, dye labels and melting temperatures only, with no amplicon sizes, repeat unit
# lengths or allele definitions, so unit_length and ref_repeats were both derived from the
# reference assembly. MLVA-8 alleles are canonically assigned from fragment size against the
# published allele table, so a derived copy number may be offset from the canonical allele by
# a constant. Confirm these values against that table, or supply it as bins.tsv, before a
# profile from this scheme is compared with published MLVA-8 genotypes.
# The unit lengths and the reference sizes are no longer only derived. Van Ert et al. 2007
# (PLoS One 2;e461), the MLVA-15 paper that carries these eight loci forward, publishes a
# repeat motif and a genomic location for each of them, and both agree with what was derived
# here: the span of every published location equals the measured ref_size exactly, the motif
# of vrrA is CAATATCAACAA, which is the stored pattern, the motif of CG3 is TAATA, a rotation
# of the same 5 bp unit and now the stored form, the motifs of pXO1-aat and pXO2-at are AAT
# and AT as stored, vrrB1 is described as a 9 bp degenerate repeat, and vrrB2, vrrC1 and vrrC2
# are described as Complex, which is what the arrays below show. The copy numbers remain
# derived, because that paper gives no allele definitions either. See the bundled scheme
# bacillus_mlva15_vanert_2007.
# How the values were established in the Ames Ancestor amplicons:
#   unit_length is the shortest period whose units tile the array; periods 2 to 60 were scored
#     by the best identity between adjacent windows. The 3 bp unit AAT of pXO1-aat and the 2 bp
#     unit AT of pXO2-at agree with the locus names, which is the only independent check the
#     source table allows.
#   ref_repeats for vrrA, vrrB1, vrrB2, CG3, pXO1-aat and pXO2-at is the count the tandem array
#     counter returns for the stored pattern at the default mismatch allowance, so the repeat
#     count cross-check is active on these six loci and check-scheme reproduces them.
#   ref_repeats for vrrC1 and vrrC2 is the number of consecutive 36 bp units in the array,
#     delimited where the identity to the preceding unit drops sharply: vrrC1 spans 7 units and
#     vrrC2 spans 8, each unit differing from its neighbour by 1 to 7 bases. No pattern is
#     stored for them because counting an array that imperfect needs a mismatch allowance that
#     would also merge unrelated windows, so their counts rest on the measurement above and the
#     cross-check is skipped rather than made to agree.
# Caveats per locus:
#   vrrA has a fifth, divergent 12 bp copy immediately upstream of the four perfect ones
#     (CAATATCGACAG, 3 differences); whether the published allele counts it is not known here.
#   vrrB1 and vrrB2 are adjacent paralogues whose amplicons overlap by 27 bp, and both hold a
#     degenerate 9 bp CA-rich repeat that runs most of the amplicon with 1 to 5 differences
#     between neighbouring units. The counts above are the clean core of each array, not its
#     full extent, so these two loci carry the largest risk of an offset. vrrB1 also shows a
#     36 bp higher-order repeat, two perfect copies of four 9 bp units plus a diverged third.
#   vrrC1 and vrrC2 are likewise adjacent paralogues, their amplicons overlapping by 36 bp,
#     exactly one repeat unit. After the seventh unit of vrrC1 the same motif continues in a
#     frame shifted by about 10 bases, which is why the array is cut there.
